original_question: Let mu(n) be the minimum size of a subset of [n] that is maximal subject to containing no 3-term arithmetic progression. Is it true that mu(4^t) = 2^t, and more generally does one always have mu(n) >= sqrt(n)?
target_in_paper: Section 2009.4.1 (Urban Larsson), the open problem "How small can a maximal AP-free set be?" and the conjecture stated there: μ(4^t)=2^t and μ(n)≥√n for all n.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual formulation. It identifies the right quantity μ(n), the right setting of maximal 3-term-arithmetic-progression-free subsets of [n], and it reproduces the two conjectural claims that are explicitly stated in the paper: μ(4^t)=2^t and μ(n)≥√n for all n.
missing_details: State that maximal means maximal with respect to inclusion among subsets of [n] that contain no 3-term arithmetic progression.
Make explicit that a 3-term arithmetic progression is nontrivial, i.e. three distinct elements x<y<z with x+z=2y.
Quantify the variables explicitly: t and n should be positive integers.

To be fully paper-faithful, note that the surrounding prose supplies the intended maximality condition; the displayed shorthand definition on the page omits it, so a stand-alone rewrite should restore it.
refined_question: For each positive integer n, let [n]={1,2,...,n}, and let μ(n) be the minimum cardinality of a subset A⊆[n] such that A contains no three distinct elements x,y,z with x+z=2y and A is maximal with respect to inclusion among subsets of [n] with that property. Is it true that μ(4^t)=2^t for every positive integer t, and more generally that μ(n)≥√n for every positive integer n?
justification: The draft is targeting exactly the Urban Larsson problem in Section 2009.4.1. The paper first asks, in prose, for the smallest maximal subset of [n] having no 3-term arithmetic progression, then introduces μ(n), gives the motivating constructions μ(3^t)≤2^t and μ(4^t)≤2^t, records the elementary lower-bound discussion, and finally states the conjecture verbatim as "I conjecture that μ(4^t)=2^t, and μ(n)≥√n for all n." The only substantive repair needed for a stand-alone formulation is to restore the maximality condition explicitly in the definition of μ(n), since the displayed shorthand formula on the page suppresses that condition even though the prose makes the intent clear.
